items.title: State can't take ownership of temple properties through gift deed: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court has held that the State government, which is legally entrusted with protecting temple properties, cannot itself take over such properties by way of a gift deed in the name of public interest or administrative convenience [K Ramalingam and Others v. Government of Tamil Nadu and Others]. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe made the observation while holding that the transfer of land belonging to the Nagapalayam Mariamman-Ponnachiamman Temple in Tamil Nadu's Erode district to the State government for the construction of a Taluk Office was illegal. The Court observed that the State's responsibility as a custodian of religious properties did not give it the authority to acquire ownership of such properties. " The State, as custodian, cannot unilaterally usurp, nor permit any of its officers to usurp, the property of the religious/charitable institutions it is charged to protect; a transaction that offends this principle, whatever its label or ostensible public purpose, is liable to be struck down, " the Court said. items.title: Calcutta High Court stays order allowing CPI(M) to set up book stall near its office
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Friday stayed a single-judge's order allowing erection of a temporary book stall by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] near its party office at the Bongaon Jessore Road. A bench of Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge and Justice Shabbar Rashidi passed the order on an appeal by the State government. The government had challenged the order passed by Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya on Thursday on a petition moved by the CPI(M). The party had alleged that the State was preventing from installing the stall Advocate Samim Ahammed, representing the CPI(M) pointed out that many people had erected their stalls in the same locality but it was only the CPI(M) members who were being obstructed. He further said that many of these stalls were being operated without proper approval. To this, the Chief Justice said, "Can there be any justification?...Just because many thieves are roaming around, I [CPI(M)] will not be caught?" CPI(M) also said that it is their fundamental duty to disseminate knowledge and information through literature and books. items.title: Children too have fundamental right to access internet; can't deny it citing online harm: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court has held that children have a fundamental right to access and use the internet and protecting them from online harm cannot justify denying them access altogether [Just Rights for Children Alliance & Anr. v. S. Harish & Ors.]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran passed the order while issuing extensive directions to detect and remove child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) online. The Court said that internet access, as a fundamental right under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution, is available to children as well as adults. “We have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. Our children, irrespective of their age enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or a freedom of speech worth expressing.
